{{Quote|Ignore the fighters! Our only concern is finding Captain Eclipse.|Boba Fett, issuing orders to the Imperial strike force|<ref name="TFU2c" />}}
A '''battle''' took place near the [[Itani Nebula/Legends|Itani Nebula]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] when an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Shadow Squadron/Legends|strike force]] launched an attack on a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Unidentified Alliance fleet|fleet]] that was hiding just outside the [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]]. After Rebel [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]] was [[Rescue of Rahm Kota|rescued]] from Imperial [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]] by [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]], the [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] late [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Galen Marek]], Starkiller and Kota traveled to where the Rebel [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] was stationed. The Rebel Alliance came under attack there from forces of the Galactic Empire commanded by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], who had first been hired by Vader to kidnap Starkiller himself. However, after failing in that task, Fett was instructed by Vader to kidnap Rebel [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], the lover of the late Marek, in order to lure Starkiller back to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], where Vader awaited.

Fett led the Empire into the rebel fleet's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] [[Salvation (flagship)|''Salvation'']], to capture Eclipse. While a [[Space warfare/Legends|battle]] ensued outside the [[Starship/Legends|starship]], another broke out between the attacking Imperials and the Rebel Alliance inside the ship. Starkiller and Kota fought through the interior of the ''Salvation'' in an attempt to rescue Eclipse, joining forces with Rebel [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] along the way. Although Starkiller and Kota defeated many Imperials, Fett escaped with his captive. Knowing that he was taking Eclipse back to Kamino, the Rebel [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|fleet]] pursued. At Kamino, the rebels and Imperials fought yet another [[Assault on Kamino|battle]] as Starkiller made his way to where Vader held Eclipse captive.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|He has a healthy head start.''"<br />"''Find the woman and bring her to me. He will follow.|Boba Fett and Darth Vader|<ref name="TFU2vg" />}}
[[File:Starkiller_Escape_Kamino.png|thumb|left|250px|Starkiller attempts to escape from Kamino.]]
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]],<ref name="TFU2c" /> [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] secretly commissioned a project on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] to [[Cloning/Legends|recreate]] his [[Death/Legends|late]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Galen Marek]]&mdash;codenamed "Starkiller." However, the accelerated cloning process was initially imperfect, thus producing [[Aberrant clone|many failed experiments]]. One clone progressed further than his precursors. Vader oversaw the [[Sith training|training]] of the clone, who was also called "[[Subject 1138|Starkiller]]." During one training session, Vader ordered Starkiller to strike down a [[Sith Training Droid|holodroid]] that was in the form of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], the lover of the original Starkiller. However, due to the [[Memory flash|emotional imprints]] that the clone genetically inherited from his [[Clone template/Legends|progenitor]], the new Starkiller had the same attraction to Eclipse that Marek had felt, so he refused to strike her down. Vader prepared to kill the clone for failing the test, but Starkiller [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|escaped]] from [[Timira City]] and set out find Juno Eclipse.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

Shortly thereafter, [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader hired the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] via a [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojector]] to track down and retrieve Starkiller. After failing to intercept him on the planet [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], Fett traveled to Kamino, where he personally met with Vader.<ref name="TFU2c" /> The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] redirected the mercenary's attention to the capture of Juno Eclipse. Vader planned to use her as bait for Starkiller to bring him back to Kamino. To infiltrate the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Unidentified Alliance fleet|fleet]] and extract Eclipse, Fett requested an entire squadron of disposable [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]; Vader responded by providing<ref name="TFU2vg" /> stormtroopers<ref name="TFU2n" /> as well as elite [[Terror Trooper]]s, [[Terror Biodroid]]s, and [[Terror Droid]]s, and a [[Terror Walker]]<ref name="TFU2vg" /> from the [[Imperial Terror Soldier]] division.<ref name="TFU2og" />

Meanwhile, Starkiller [[Rescue of Rahm Kota|rescued]] Rebel [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]] from [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]] on Cato Neimoidia. Following clues he had obtained, Starkiller went to the planet [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]], where he met [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]&ndash;in&ndash;[[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]. Entering a [[Cave of Evil/Legends|cave]], Starkiller had a [[Force vision/Legends|Force vision]] of Eclipse being attacked on the Rebel [[Starship/Legends|ship]] [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] [[Salvation (flagship)|''Salvation'']]. Back outside, Yoda gave Starkiller advice on what to do in relation to his vision, and Starkiller left Dagobah to retrieve Kota,<ref name="TFU2vg" /> whom he had left on the planet [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] before going to Dagobah.<ref name="TFU2n" /> Reunited, the pair went to the location of the Rebel [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|fleet]] near the [[Itani Nebula/Legends|Itani Nebula]]; Starkiller hoped to get to Eclipse before his vision came to fruition.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

==The battle==
{{Quote|Stay on guard. A powerful glimpse of the future like you experienced is rarely wrong.|Rahm Kota, to Starkiller, concerning the latter's vision of the Rebel fleet under attack|<ref name="TFU2vg" />}}
[[File:Salvation_fleet.png|thumb|left|250px|The ''Salvation'' near the Itani Nebula.]]
By the [[Time/Legends|time]] Starkiller and Kota reached the Rebel [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]], Fett had also succeeded in discovering that the Rebel [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] ''Salvation'', under the command of Captain Eclipse, was located amongst the fleet's [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. Just as the clone and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] landed the starship ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'' on Eclipse's ship, Fett and the Imperials under his control&mdash;[[Shadow Squadron (Itani Nebula)|Shadow Squadron]], including [[Shadow Leader]] and [[Shadow One]]&mdash;launched their surprise attack. The battle began with an Imperial [[Space warfare/Legends|attack]] on the Rebel ships and [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]]<ref name="TFU2c" />&mdash;which included the [[Bomber/Legends|assault bomber]] [[Lexi Dio (starship)|''Lexi Dio'']], the first vessel to be destroyed along with all of its crew<ref name="TFU2n" />&mdash;[[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighters]], at least one [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]], a couple of [[DP20 gunship/Legends|DP20 frigates]], and an [[Action VI bulk transport/Legends|Action VI transport]]. The [[TIE starfighter]]s launched [[breaching pod]]s into the ''Salvation'', and the Imperials entered and secured several decks of the starship. The [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunter then entered the ''Salvation'' and proceeded to the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] with an escort of Terror [[Trooper/Legends|Troopers]]<ref name="TFU2c" /> and [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="TFU2n" /> In the ensuing [[Lightfight|firefight]], many Rebels were killed, the [[Holodroid/Legends|holodroid]] [[PROXY]] was severely damaged, and Eclipse was captured by Fett. The bounty hunter, Eclipse in tow, made his way to his personal ship, the [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft/Legends|''Firespray-31''-class patrol and attack craft]] [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']], which he had used to reach the ''Salvation''.<ref name="TFU2c" />

Meanwhile, using their [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], Starkiller and Kota fought their way through the corridors of the ''Salvation'' to reach the bridge where Fett had captured Eclipse. Starkiller found PROXY on the bridge, and the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] updated him on the situation. Upon finding out that Fett had taken Eclipse to the [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]], Starkiller pursued as Kota went to order an attack on the Imperial cloning facilities on the planet Kamino. Traveling through much of the starship, Starkiller fought against the Terror Troopers, Terror Droids, Terror Biodroids,<ref name="TFU2vg" /> and stormtroopers<ref name="TFU2n" /> that were at Fett's disposal, assisting [[Rebel trooper/Legends|Rebel troopers]] along the way. Kota, meanwhile, kept in contact with Starkiller via [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]]. Eventually, Starkiller spotted Eclipse being taken away by Fett. Starkiller battled through the ''Salvation'', even going through the inner-workings of the ship, to reach the docking bay before Fett could depart;<ref name="TFU2vg" /> Fett and Eclipse were heading for the ''Slave I'', which was positioned just outside the ''Salvation''. Starkiller attempted to use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to [[Telekinesis/Legends|retrieve]] Eclipse, but he failed due to an attack by a giant droid known as the Terror Walker. After a brief battle, the Terror Droid fell through several decks of the ''Salvation''. However, Starkiller was too late; Fett had jumped to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] with his captive. The TIE fighters then escaped as well.<ref name="TFU2n" />

Infuriated at not being able to stop the bounty hunter, Starkiller ordered Kota to attack Kamino. Kota had already done so, and the Rebel ships prepared for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]].<ref name="TFU2vg" /> Starkiller then experienced another Force vision, one that regarded a possible outcome in the imminent future. On the [[Water/Legends|rain]]-soaked facility of [[Timira City]], Starkiller witnessed his own death at the hands of a [[Dark Apprentice|fellow clone of Galen Marek]]. Unlike himself and the many failures that Vader had created, the dream clone was the perfect version that Vader intended to use as Marek's replacement. After awakening from the vision, Starkiller knew that defeat was in his future if he gave in once more to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="TFU2n" />

Starkiller then realized that the Terror Walker was going for the ship's secondary [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]], and he needed to stop it. Although much of the crew had been disabled during the attack, Kota sent some Rebel [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] to assist Starkiller, but they were killed.<ref name="TFU2n" /> Starkiller fought the Terror Walker once more&mdash;along with more Terror Droids, Terror Biodroids, and Terror Troopers.<ref name="TFU2vg" /> During the battle, the droid punctured a hole in the side of the ship. With some assistance from Starkiller, the Terror Walker was forced out into the depths of hyperspace, and Starkiller returned to the ship's bridge.<ref name="TFU2n" />

==Aftermath==
[[File:Titan_Droid_TFU2_E3.png|thumb|right|250px|Starkiller attacks the Terror Walker.]]
{{Quote|Hope you're ready for a fight.''"<br />"''My Star Destroyers will wipe out the Rebel ships. And the planetary shields will prevent ground troops from landing. But Starkiller ''will'' find a way onto the planet. Of this, I am certain.|Boba Fett and Darth Vader|<ref name="TFU2c" />}}
Boba Fett arrived on the planet Kamino and delivered Eclipse to Vader.<ref name="TFU2c" /> Shortly thereafter, the Rebel fleet arrived at Kamino, but the Empire was waiting for them. The [[Assault on Kamino|Battle of Kamino]] ensued, and Starkiller went down to the surface of the watery world. He traveled through the cloning facilities and finally arrived where Vader was holding Eclipse. After a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]], Starkiller defeated Vader, thus rescuing Eclipse. The Rebels won the Battle of Kamino, and they subsequently took Vader into custody.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Whoever this bounty hunter is, he brought friends.|Rahm Kota, about Boba Fett and the Imperials, in the Nintendo DS version of the game|<ref name="TFU2vg" />}}
The battle first appeared in the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (graphic novel)|comic adaption]] of the [[2010]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''. In the game, it appears as a playable level. The battle also appears in the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|novelization]] of the game, written by [[Sean Williams]]. The [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] version of the game concentrates more on the events surrounding Boba Fett, rather than those concerning Starkiller. While the [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]], [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]], and [[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]]/[[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PlayStation 3]] versions of the game differ from each other, the storyline remains basically the same. This article follows the Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version, since it remains closer to the novel, itself considered to enjoy a higher level of [[canon]]icity.<ref name="canon">{{SWArchive|url=vault/books/tfu2_books/index.html?page=1|text=This Week: Experience ''The Force Unleashed II'' Story in Books}}</ref> The novel differs from the Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version of the game in several ways. Stormtroopers are mentioned as part of the fighting force of the Imperials, while there are no stormtroopers included in the battle in the Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version. The novel also expounds on the overall story more than the game, focusing more on Juno Eclipse's experience than the game does. The novel also includes a sequence where Starkiller uses the Force to attempt to rescue Eclipse from Fett when they make their escape towards the ''Slave I''. However, in the Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 game, Starkiller merely arrives just as the ''Slave I'' is leaving the ''Salvation''. Also, Starkiller has a brief vision in the book shortly after Fett escapes, but this is exempt from the game. The Terror Walker is destroyed in the novel by being sucked out into hyperspace. However, Starkiller actually physically destroys it in the game, and the droid does not leave the ship.

In the Wii version of the game, Starkiller and Kota get separated on their way to the bridge of the ''Salvation'', and they regroup at the bridge. However, in both the novel and Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version, no such separation occurs. Similar to the novel, the Wii version has stormtroopers involved in the attack. Although Starkiller chases Fett and Eclipse in the Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version, the chase is much more involved in the Wii version. The trip through the ''Salvation'' differs slightly, and Starkiller comes in close contact and fights Fett at times. Like the novel, Starkiller attempts to stop Fett and Eclipse via the Force when they try to leave in the ''Slave I''. Also like the novel, the Terror Walker arrives, Fett escapes with Eclipse, and the battle with the droid begins. The Terror Walker battle follows a different story than the other adaptions. Starkiller chases the Terror Walker through the core of the starship, and he must fix the core, which the droid had damaged, before actually fighting the mechanical enemy. While the ''Salvation'' has already made the jump to hyperspace by the time of the Terror Droid battle in the novel and Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version, Starkiller must defeat the Terror Walker in a certain amount of time in the Wii version, as he will be killed if the ship jumps to hyperspace while he is in the location where he fights the droid. In the cutscene after the battle in the Wii version, Starkiller leaves the area after Kota warns him that the ''Salvation'' will be leaving for Hyperspace "with or without [Starkiller]", with the Terror Walker struggling to move before being sucked into the hyperdrive core.

The DS version is played in [[Wikipedia:2D computer graphics|2D mode]], rather than in the [[Wikipedia:3D computer graphics|3D style]] of the other versions of the game. The story follows the basic storyline of the Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version. In the DS version, Starkiller faces stormtroopers, as he does in the novel. Like the Xbox 360/PlayStation 3 version, Starkiller chases Fett and Eclipse through the ''Salvation'', but he arrives just as the ''Slave I'' is leaving; Starkiller does not use the Force in an attempt to bring the ship back as he does in other adaptions.
